title: Wish, if only and regrets
what: using 'would' or the simple past wrongly after 'wish' ('I wish I would have more time', 'I wish I didn't say that')
summary: This error persists because it mirrors conditional structures, making it feel intuitively correct. However, it subtly undermines the speaker's command of nuanced regret and hypothetical situations.
listenFor: Pay close attention to the verb tense immediately following 'wish' or 'if only' when expressing a desire or regret about the present or past.

contrasts.wrong: I wish I would have a clearer understanding of the project scope.
contrasts.right: I wish I had a clearer understanding of the project scope.
contrasts.note: Use past simple for present desires.

contrasts.wrong: I wish I didn't miss that crucial deadline last week.
contrasts.right: I wish I hadn't missed that crucial deadline last week.
contrasts.note: Use past perfect for past regrets.

contrasts.wrong: I wish I didn't invest so much in that volatile stock.
contrasts.right: I wish I hadn't invested so much in that volatile stock.
contrasts.note: Use past perfect for past regrets.

contrasts.wrong: I wish my commute would be shorter every morning.
contrasts.right: I wish my commute were shorter every morning.
contrasts.note: Use past subjunctive for hypothetical present states.

contrasts.wrong: If only I didn't accept that challenging assignment.
contrasts.right: If only I hadn't accepted that challenging assignment.
contrasts.note: Use past perfect for past regrets.

drills: I wish I had more time to dedicate to professional development.
If only I knew the answer to that complex problem.
I wish I hadn't overlooked those critical details in the report.
She wishes she were able to travel more for work.
We wish we had anticipated the market shift sooner.
He wishes he hadn't made that impulsive decision about his career.
If only they understood the implications of their proposal.
I wish I had saved more money during my early career.
They wish they hadn't signed the contract without legal review.
If only I were fluent in another language for international business.

probes.sentence: I wish I would be able to attend the conference next month.
answers: I wish I were able to attend the conference next month.
I wish I could attend the conference next month.

probes.sentence: If only I didn't forget to submit the expense report on time.
answers: If only I hadn't forgotten to submit the expense report on time.

probes.sentence: He wishes he would have a better work-life balance.
answers: He wishes he had a better work-life balance.

probes.sentence: If only I didn't agree to work overtime every weekend.
answers: If only I hadn't agreed to work overtime every weekend.
